facts.fact: The false-bottomed teak chest in Ittan's lead cart holds thirty-six blank split-ash tally sticks wrapped in oilcloth, each with council wax bearing the dot-and-split mark, plus a hand-sized oilcloth tally book of about forty leaves recording dated sums and pass place-names.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires blank pass-tokens in council wax and Ittan's private tally to be found.

facts.fact: Devan carries Asha's first token and his beeswax impression in his sleeve, and compares them to the chest's wax on sealing day; the dot-and-split mark matches.
facts.why: needed because the beat says the wax impression matches the token from Asha's chest.

facts.fact: Neela tells the court the slip was torn from a courier's papers by someone now dead, whom Devan declines to name.
facts.why: needed to produce Chathu's slip publicly without exposing Ammu's name or the guild.

facts.fact: Ittan is held in the padippura guardroom, and the warden's seal is an iron disc cut with a hill and a gate, worn by eleven wardens.
facts.why: needed to stage the arrest and the sealing.
